behavioral_notes.observation: Agreement lifecycle is draft -> confirmed -> done(Closed) / cancel; the agreement itself has no RFQ/PO sub-states. action_confirm refuses an empty agreement, and for requisition_type='blanket_order' validates every line has price_unit>0 and product_qty>0, then calls line._create_supplier_info() to publish vendor prices before setting state='confirmed'. action_done ('Close') raises if any linked purchase.order is still draft/sent/'to approve' (you must cancel open RFQs first), then unlinks the published supplierinfo and sets state='done'. action_cancel cancels all linked POs (button_cancel) and removes the supplierinfo. Not visible in metadata.

requisition_type Selection drives behaviour and naming: 'blanket_order' is a negotiated price+quantity agreement that feeds product.supplierinfo and tracks qty_ordered against the agreed amount; 'purchase_template' is a reusable product list with no committed price/qty. create()/write() select the ir.sequence ('purchase.requisition.blanket.order' vs '...purchase.template') accordingly, and changing type/company on a non-draft agreement raises UserError. _compute_price_unit only auto-prices purchase_template lines (via product._select_seller); blanket lines keep their negotiated price. Encoded in Python, not metadata.

For a confirmed blanket order, each line creates a product.supplierinfo (sudo) carrying the agreement vendor, product, UoM, negotiated price and currency, back-linked via purchase_requisition_line_id. Editing the line price propagates to that supplierinfo (write -> supplier_info_ids.write({'price':...})), and price<=0 on an active blanket order is rejected. product.product._prepare_sellers then filters sellers so a PO tied to a requisition only sees that requisition's supplierinfo (plus unscoped ones) -- this is the mechanism by which a blanket agreement automatically becomes the vendor price applied on generated purchase orders.

behavioral_notes.element: purchase.order._onchange_requisition_id (generating a purchase order from an agreement)
behavioral_notes.observation: Selecting an Agreement on a draft purchase.order copies vendor, currency, company, fiscal position, payment term, note and date_order from the requisition, appends the agreement name to origin, and seeds order_line from the agreement's line_ids (mapping taxes through the fiscal position). Quantity defaults to the agreement line qty for purchase_template but to 0 for blanket_order (drawn down on demand). PO line price/date/name are later re-derived from the matched requisition line in _compute_price_unit_and_date_planned_and_name. This is the agreement -> purchase.order materialisation, absent from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: purchase.order.group + alternative_po_ids (call for tenders / competing RFQs)
behavioral_notes.observation: 'Call for tender' is implemented not as an agreement state but through purchase.order.group: action_create_alternative spawns competing RFQs to other vendors (create_alternative wizard, optionally copying products) linked via a shared purchase.order.group that auto-creates and auto-implodes when <=1 PO remains. action_compare_alternative_lines + get_tender_best_lines compute the best price / best price-unit / earliest-date line per product, and action_choose/action_clear_quantities zero the losing lines. button_confirm intercepts confirmation while open alternatives exist, popping purchase.requisition.alternative.warning to keep or cancel the rival RFQs (skip_alternative_check bypass). Pure-Python orchestration over the PO model.

3 JS files, 0 OWL components, 2 registry adds (fields:many2many_alt_pos, views:purchase_order_line_compare), 0 patches; bundle ['web.assets_backend'] (4). The alternative-PO field widget + order-line compare list are the only client surfaces; no portal/public assets.

it_architecture.application: purchase_requisition (Purchase Agreements extension of the Purchase application component)
information_flows: side-effect: purchase.requisition.action_confirm (blanket) -> product.supplierinfo (vendor price agreement published)
side-effect: purchase.order._onchange_requisition_id -> purchase.order.line (PO seeded from agreement lines; taxes/price/dates from agreement)
side-effect: product.product._prepare_sellers -> agreement-scoped supplierinfo applied to requisition-linked POs
side-effect: purchase.order.action_create_alternative -> purchase.order.group (competing RFQs grouped for tender comparison)
side-effect: purchase.requisition.action_done -> blocks while linked POs are draft/sent/to-approve, then unlinks supplierinfo

capabilities: Manage Purchase Agreements (blanket orders & purchase templates)
Call for Tenders / Competing RFQ Management
value_streams: Source-to-Agreement: agreement draft -> confirm (blanket price published) -> draw-down POs -> close
Call-for-tender: origin RFQ -> alternative RFQs (group) -> compare best lines -> award one / cancel rivals
policies: 2 record rules: multi-company scoping on purchase.requisition + purchase.requisition.line
blanket-order integrity: lines require price>0 & qty>0 to confirm; price<=0 rejected on an active blanket order
no agreement-type/company change on a non-draft agreement; delete only draft/cancelled agreements
close (action_done) blocked while linked RFQs/POs remain open (draft/sent/to approve)
group_purchase_alternatives feature flag (res.config.settings.group_purchase_alternatives) gates the alternatives UI
stakeholders: Strategic sourcing / category buyer (runs tenders & blanket negotiations)
metrics: purchase.requisition.line.qty_ordered (drawn-down vs agreed quantity per blanket line)
purchase.requisition.order_count (number of POs generated from an agreement)
tender best price / best price-unit / earliest date per product (get_tender_best_lines)

classification.rationale: purchase_requisition is a procurement support extension (strategic sourcing) layered on the purchase application: it depends only on purchase and adds no primary transform. It supports the value chain upstream by negotiating blanket-order price agreements (published as product.supplierinfo that downstream POs draw on) and by running call-for-tenders that compare competing RFQs to award the best vendor. Per Stabell & Fjeldstad it is a support activity (procurement/sourcing) provisioning inputs for the primary activities. Maps to APQC 4.2 Procure Materials and Services -- specifically 4.2.4 (manage tenders/agreements: alternative RFQ comparison + blanket orders) and the source-side 4.2.1.1 Develop procurement plan (per the APQC<->Odoo map, purchase.requisition is the requisition/agreement evidence).

standard_capabilities: blanket orders (negotiated price + quantity agreement with a vendor)
purchase templates (reusable product list for fast RFQ/PO creation)
agreement -> product.supplierinfo price publication feeding purchase orders
agreement-seeded purchase orders (vendor/terms/lines copied on selection)
call for tenders: competing alternative RFQs grouped via purchase.order.group
alternative-quote comparison with best price / unit / date selection and quantity clearing
blanket draw-down tracking (qty_ordered vs agreed qty)
typical_fits: long-term blanket agreement with a single vendor at a fixed negotiated price
purchase template for recurring baskets of products
multi-vendor tender with best-line award and automatic loser cancellation
common_gaps: no agreement-level approval/sign-off workflow (only blanket line validation + PO double-validation inherited from purchase)
tender scoring limited to price/unit/date heuristics (no weighted multi-criteria vendor scoring)
no portal/EDI surface for vendors to submit tender bids (backend-only; 0 routes)
no automatic blanket-quantity ceiling enforcement on draw-down POs
supplier contract terms / renewal management beyond date_start/date_end
